title: Internal playbook prioritization and risk heatmap
summary: Working session to prioritize playbook items for next month, align canary rollout charter, and map the risk heatmap for the upcoming private deployment launch. Actionable owners and tentative dates recorded; decision to run a two-week canary with staged traffic pacing. Noted gaps in rollback automation and KV cache eviction observability.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-01 10:00 PT / Duration ~78 minutes / Attendees listed above

Summary (auto): quick planning, risk map, assign owners, set timeline for canary and follow-up bench runs.

[00:00] Priya Shah: okay, good morning everyone. Let's kick off, I wanted to run through the playbook backlog and then carve out the canary charter. We have 11 items, roughly, um, and we need to pick the top five for the two week window.
[00:22] Liam Chen: got it. Quick note, yesterday we saw a flaky eviction in the staging kv cache test — not the same as the OOM but it's uh, correlated with long tails under concurrent small requests. Might impact canary stability.
[00:37] Sofia Martinez: yeah I looked at that, there's a race in the eviction path when we run multiple batching windows. My gut is we need a guard in the runtime to prevent double-evict.
[00:52] Ethan Brooks: and we still lack a good synthetic that reproduces the per-token latency tail — our current bench spikes only at 2x load, but the real world shows 1.3x with microbursts.
[01:10] Priya Shah: so that's an observability/bench gap. Add it to the heatmap under medium-high. Carlos, can you capture market/regulatory risk?
[01:21] Carlos Reyes: sure, but it's... ok, regulatory chatter is low for the private deploy for now, customers ask about e2e encryption and audit logs. We'll flag SOC2 docs as prerequisite for enterprise pilots.
[01:34] Priya Shah: noted.
[01:36] Jamal Ortiz: quick data point from QA — our canary test harness doesn't replay real session prefixes, so caches look colder than they will be in prod. We'll need a prefix priming job.
[01:50] Nina Patel: that's critical because we rely on prefix/KV caching to hit our latency SLO in many cases.
[01:58] Priya Shah: alright, let's walk through the playbook list. Item one: canary rollout charter. Item two: rollback automation — add a runbook + CI gating. Item three: checkpointing KV cache before rollout. Item four: burst traffic shaping policy. Item five: obs dashboards for token tail. Then lower priority: dependency pinning, quantization profile checks, licensing audit, perf regression harness, and cross-region fallback test.
[02:27] Liam Chen: for rollback automation, SEs need an API to peel traffic per pool and a safe abort hook. We can reuse the existing router feature flag but it doesn't handle kv cache invalidation, so state can be stale after rollback.
[02:45] Sofia Martinez: that's the vulnerability — stale KV means incorrect completions if we switch models mid-request. We should treat KV invalidation as atomic with rollback or provide a compatibility shim.
[02:58] Ethan Brooks: shim might be faster short-term: provide a compatibility layer that accepts old cache keys but marks them degraded. But long-term we need atomic migration tooling.
[03:12] Priya Shah: decision note: immediate fix = compatibility shim + explicit cache invalidation step in rollback runbook. Long-term = atomic migration work in Q3. Marked as medium-high risk.
[03:23] Carlos Reyes: timeline question — when do we want to start the canary? Customer pilots are asking for mid-May, so we should be ready for a canary mid-April to validate infra assumptions. That gives two weeks for canary and one week for follow-ups.
[03:39] Priya Shah: scheduling constraint: release window is tight. Nina, any calendar conflicts or other release priorities?
[03:46] Nina Patel: there is a separate infra maintenance window on April 20th that might overlap; let's avoid that. We can start canary April 13th through April 27th ideally.
[03:55] Jamal Ortiz: note — QA needs at least three full days to run the priming and prefix replay after we land the harness. So land earlier.
[04:06] Priya Shah: ok plan: ship harness April 9th, start canary April 13th. Two-week canary with staged traffic increase: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% (over 10 business days).
[04:22] Sofia Martinez: checkpoint idea: before each stage increase, run a short 'health sweep' against a subset of latency-critical endpoints and assert no regressed p95. If p95 regresses more than 15% we auto-hold.
[04:36] Ethan Brooks: and tie that to a circuit-breaker that can throttle traffic back to previous stage automatically. We'll need a safe hold TTL and manual override.
[04:46] Priya Shah: good. Put TTL default to 15 minutes then escalate to on-call if manual override not resolved.
[04:54] Liam Chen: about observability — we need token-level tracing for the canary. Current tracing drops token attribution when we batch. Is anyone working on that?
[05:03] Sofia Martinez: partially — there's an open PR but it's not merged; it gets tricky with continuous batching. I can expedite.
[05:12] Priya Shah: expedite please.
[05:13] Carlos Reyes: competitors note: if we delay, customers may test other providers (Anthropic, Cohere's inference endpoints) — not critical for internal timeline but something to watch when we hit pilot.
[05:26] Jamal Ortiz: another QA note: flakey tests in the perf harness are hiding transient GC spikes. It'd be useful to add a synthetic that simulates small chat bursts with mixed short and long context.
[05:40] Ethan Brooks: can we reuse the replay infra from the streaming team? They have a session replayer but it's built around a different protocol. Might be friction.
[05:49] Sofia Martinez: we should prototype an adapter rather than rebuild.
[05:53] Priya Shah: action: Sofia + Jamal to prototype adapter by April 6th. (we'll capture in next steps).
[06:00] -- Transcript jumps ahead, discussion moves into risk heatmap details --
[06:05] Priya Shah: let's populate the risk heatmap matrix: columns = likelihood, impact, mitigation, owner. Row 1 = rollback failure due to stale KV, likelihood = medium, impact = high, mitigation = shim + invalidation + gating, owner = Liam/Sofia.
[06:28] Liam Chen: Row 2 = canary instability from spike tails, likelihood = high if we don't prime cache, impact = medium-high. Mitigation = prefix priming job + synthetic microburst harness. Owner = Jamal/Ethan.
[06:44] Sofia Martinez: Row 3 = lack of observability for token-level p95 -> likelihood medium, impact high, mitigation = token tracing + dashboards, owner = Sofia.
[06:57] Priya Shah: Row 4 = compliance docs not ready for pilots -> likelihood low-medium, impact medium, mitigation = compile SOC2 artifacts and legal readout, owner = Carlos.
[07:12] Carlos Reyes: I can get an initial SOC2 pack by April 20th but will need security to sign off.
[07:20] Priya Shah: add that.
[07:23] -- Slight cross-talk, discussion on who signs off for go/no-go --
[07:30] Nina Patel: go/no-go gating: perf SLOs, no sev for 72 hours at stage 20%+, security checklist complete, rollback automation validated. These are musts.
[07:44] Priya Shah: agreed. 
[07:46] Liam Chen: question about metrics retention — for the canary we need extended retention for detailed token traces for 30 days. That costs $$$. Who signs the budget?
[07:58] Carlos Reyes: we can fund initial 30-day retention from marketing pilot budget; but we need a cost estimate. I will follow up.
[08:08] Priya Shah: Carlos to estimate by EOD Friday April 2.
[08:12] -- Discussion about test plan and owners --
[08:20] Jamal Ortiz: for the prefix priming job, we need a dataset of real session prefixes scrubbed for PII. Do we have a scrubbed seed?
[08:31] Sofia Martinez: there's an old scrubbed corpus from last year but it's small. We should combine it with synthetic variations. Jamal + QA, please curate by April 6.
[08:41] Jamal Ortiz: noted.
[08:43] Priya Shah: let's move to decision log: decisions made so far: 1) start canary April 13th; 2) immediate cache shim + invalidation required; 3) prefix priming harness; 4) staged traffic with health sweep gating; 5) token-level tracing expedited.
[09:00] Nina Patel: add a decision: hold canary if infra maintenance on April 20th overlaps — avoid that window unless maintenance is rescheduled.
[09:10] -- Mid-call note: brief tangent about Dedicated vs Hosted behavior --
[09:17] Liam Chen: small thing — dedicated pools behave slightly differently with autoscale; we must ensure the canary test uses both dedicated and hosted model variants for coverage.
[09:28] Priya Shah: ok, include both in the canary matrix.
[09:31] Carlos Reyes: also call out quantization profile differences — some customers will want int8 profiles, which change perf curves. We should run an int8 smoke test in week two.
[09:44] Sofia Martinez: that might be lower priority but we can schedule a quick run.
[09:48] Priya Shah: schedule int8 smoke test for April 22nd if possible.
[09:52] -- Later discussion about incident retro and backlog grooming --
[10:00] Liam Chen: retrospective note — last incident route: kernel fallback logic didn't surface a clear metric for invocation count, so ops couldn't correlate rollback with increased fallbacks. We need a dedicated metric.
[10:14] Ethan Brooks: I'll add a fallback_invocations counter and a sampled trace to correlate with request ids.
[10:22] Priya Shah: thanks. That helps us for post-canary analysis.
[10:26] -- Closing, recap and next steps --
[10:30] Priya Shah: recap: owners and dates. I'll send a follow-up doc with the charter. We agreed on April 9th harness, April 13th canary start, two weeks duration with staged traffic. Immediate owners: Sofia+Jamal (prefix priming adapter) due Apr 6; Ethan+Jamal (synthetic microburst harness) due Apr 7; Sofia expedite token tracing by Apr 5; Liam+Sofia implement shim + invalidation by Apr 8; Carlos estimate retention cost by Apr 2; Nina to confirm no infra conflict by Apr 3; Carlos to compile SOC2 pack draft by Apr 20.
[10:55] Carlos Reyes: I'll also prepare a short pilot go-to-market note for customers.
[11:00] Priya Shah: excellent. Any blockers?
[11:03] Sofia Martinez: merge backlog and prioritization conflicts with Q3 work; we might need to shuffle.
[11:09] Priya Shah: we will escalate if needed. Thanks everyone, meeting adjourned.

Action Items (recorded in transcript): Sofia + Jamal: prototype adapter for replay by 2026-04-06; Ethan + Jamal: synthetic microburst harness by 2026-04-07; Sofia: token tracing expedited by 2026-04-05; Liam + Sofia: cache shim + invalidation by 2026-04-08; Carlos: retention cost estimate by 2026-04-02; Nina: confirm infra window by 2026-04-03; Carlos: SOC2 pack draft by 2026-04-20.

References mentioned: internal charters (link: /docs/canary-charter) — note: doc stub will be created after meeting. Bench spreadsheets & perf harness (link: /sheets/canary-bench), SOC2 checklist (link: /security/soc2-checklist).
